algorithms.name: UCB (tuned, exploration log(t)+c log log t)

extra_assumptions: c = 3 in exploration function log(t)+c log log(t)

source.label: th:borneRegret
source.quote: Consider a bandit problem with $K$ arms and independent rewards bounded in $[0,1]$, and denote by $a^*$ an optimal arm. Choosing $c=3$, the regret of the KL-UCB algorithm satisfies: \[\limsup_{n\to\infty} \frac{\E[R_n]}{\log(n)} \leq \sum_{a:\mu_a<\mu_{a^*}} \frac{\mu_{a^*}-\mu_a}{d(\mu_a, \mu_{a^*})}\;.\]

results.notes: Bound is limsup of E[R_n]/log(n). d is Bernoulli KL even for general [0,1] rewards. Index uses log t, so horizon-free/anytime.

bound.regime: any positive integer n, any eps > 0

symbols.C_1: positive constant (proof indicates related to C'_1 <= 7 plus 3(1+eps)/kl term)
symbols.C_2: positive function C_2(epsilon) of epsilon, O(epsilon^-2)

source.label: th:borneNbplayed
source.quote: Let $\epsilon>0$, and take $c=3$ in Algorithm~\ref{alg:klUCB}. ... For any positive integer $n$, the number of times algorithm KL-UCB chooses arm $a$ is upper-bounded by \[\E[N_n(a)] \leq \frac{\log(n)}{d(\mu_a, \mu_{a^*})}(1+\epsilon) + C_1 \log(\log(n)) + \frac{C_2(\epsilon)}{n^{\beta(\epsilon)}}\;,\]

results.notes: Quantity is expected number of pulls of a single suboptimal arm a (kl_i with i=a).
Expected number of draws of suboptimal arm a, normalized by log n.

bound.regime: any positive integer n, any eps > 0

extra_assumptions: c = 3; UCB index S[a]/N[a] + sqrt((log t + c log log t)/(2N[a]))

source.label: prop:betterUCB
source.quote: Consider the UCB algorithm tuned as follows: at step $t>K$, the arm that maximizes the upper-bound $S[a]/N[a] + \sqrt{(\log(t)+c\log\log(t))/(2 N[a])}$ is chosen. Then, for the choice $c=3$, the number of draws of a sub-optimal arm $a$ is upper-bounded as: \E[N_n(a)] \leq \frac{\log(n)}{2(\mu_a-\mu_{a^*})^2}(1+\epsilon) + C_1 \log(\log(n)) + \frac{C_2(\epsilon)}{n^{\beta(\epsilon)}}

results.notes: Proof omitted in paper (mimics KL-UCB proof with quadratic divergence). Bound on expected pulls of suboptimal arm. The paper's statement has 2(...)^2 denominator, i.e. 1/(2 Delta^2) as printed.

source.quote: If the reward distributions are Bernoulli, the KL-UCB algorithm is asymptotically optimal, in the sense that the regret of KL-UCB matches the lower-bound proved by~\cite{LaiRobbins85bandits} and generalized by~\cite{BurnetasKatehakis97bandits}: \[N_n(a) \geq \left( \frac{1}{d(\mu_a, \mu_{a^*})} + o(1) \right)\log(n)\] with a probability tending to $1$.

results.notes: Corollary asserts asymptotic optimality for Bernoulli rewards; the upper bound is Theorem 1 specialised, matching the Lai-Robbins constant (lower bound itself recorded as cited).

extra_assumptions: divergence d replaced by the exponential-family rate function, which equals KL(p_{mu^-1(x)}, p_{mu^-1(y)}) by Lemma 1

source.quote: Then, all the results stated above apply (as the proofs do not involve the particular form of the function $d$), and in particular~: \[\limsup_{n\to\infty} \frac{\E[R_n]}{\log(n)} \leq \sum_{a:\mu_a<\mu_{a^*}} \frac{\mu_{a^*}-\mu_a}{d(\mu_a, \mu_{a^*})}\;.\]

results.notes: Stated informally in text, not as a numbered theorem; proof sketched by reference to the bounded case and Theorem 5 (deviation bound, proof omitted). d equals KL within the family, so KL_i used.
